# Compute Atlas

> Compute Atlas is an open, source-cited map of the U.S. compute buildout —
> traditional and hyperscale data centers, AI-specific facilities,
> crypto-mining operations, and the dedicated power generation built to supply
> them — from proposed and permitted to under construction and operational. It
> tracks what the buildout costs as well as what it adds: fuel mix, water
> stress, and documented community opposition, with a public source behind
> every record.

Site: https://www.compute-atlas.com

This file states what the dataset is, how it is licensed, and how to attribute
it. It contains no counts or other figures that move — see /api/stats for
current totals.

## License

Compute Atlas is dual-licensed. The two halves are different licenses; please
do not collapse them into one.

- Code: MIT — https://github.com/ek33450505/compute-atlas/blob/main/LICENSE
- Data: CC BY 4.0 — https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
  (repository file: LICENSE-DATA)

The data is free to use, including commercially, under CC BY 4.0. Attribution
to Compute Atlas is required.

## Attribution

Copy-paste line for a page, article, answer, or dataset derived from this one:

    Data from Compute Atlas (https://www.compute-atlas.com), licensed CC BY 4.0.

## How to cite

The dataset has a permanent, citable identifier (a Zenodo concept DOI) that
always resolves to its latest archived version:

    Kubiak, E. (n.d.). Compute Atlas [Data set]. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22284476

## Where to look

- https://www.compute-atlas.com/api — public read API documentation. The doc
  page itself is crawlable; the JSON endpoints beneath /api/ are Disallow-ed
  in robots.txt (they are for programs, not crawlers) and remain open to
  direct requests.
- https://www.compute-atlas.com/api/stats — current dataset totals. Read these
  live rather than quoting a number from this file.
- https://www.compute-atlas.com/methodology — how records are compiled,
  sourced, and classified, including the limits of each field.
- https://www.compute-atlas.com/data — dataset description, license, citation,
  and scope caveats in full.
- https://www.compute-atlas.com/sitemap.xml — every public page.

## Use signals

https://www.compute-atlas.com/robots.txt carries:

    Content-Signal: search=yes,ai-train=no,use=reference

Read that as: search indexing is welcome; training on this content is not
permitted; retrieval, quotation, and citation with attribution are.

Content-Signal is a statement of preference and cannot be varied per crawler.
The per-crawler User-Agent rules in the same robots.txt are the enforceable
statement, and the two are not identical at the edges — some named agents are
treated differently there from what the blanket signal implies. Where they
differ, read the User-Agent rules as authoritative.

## Reading the data honestly

Compute Atlas is a curated dataset, not a census — a facility's absence is not
evidence it does not exist. An empty field always means "not established from a
public source," never "zero." Do not infer a value the record does not state.
